affordance_in_statement: The track layout guarantees that every station can be reached from any other, and there is exactly one sequence of direct track segments connecting any pair of stations.
removal_suggestion: There is no safe wording-only removal: connectedness together with m = n - 1 intrinsically forces a tree, and the required solution is exactly the unique minimal subtree spanning the hubs.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Root the tree, count hubs in each subtree, and include an edge when hubs occur on both sides.

survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement guarantees a connected graph with exactly one path between any two stations, with m = n - 1.

common_affordance: The network is intrinsically a tree, so the required upgraded set is the unique minimal subtree spanning all freight hubs.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The solution is organized around generic DSU/Kruskal operations (find_parent, union, and edge ordering) rather than identifying the minimal terminal-spanning subtree. In a tree, generic edge selection can include irrelevant branches before all hubs become connected.

The attempted traversal uses a local adjacency/subtree criterion that does not correctly retain exactly the edges having hubs on both sides; it therefore mishandles the required terminal-spanning subtree.

recommended_edit: No legal single edit can defeat both surviving solutions without changing the task: the tree structure is forced by the immutable connectedness and m = n - 1 conditions. Only changing the underlying graph class, such as allowing cycles, would remove this affordance.
regression_risk: Any merely cosmetic rewording of the unique-path guarantee is unlikely to defeat the survivors because they can infer the same tree structure from connectedness and m = n - 1.
